# Proving you're human shouldn't require an eyeball scanner. | André F. · LinkedIn · 2026-04-06

**André F.**: Founder and CEO at Incognia for 5 years 11 months with 15 years 1 month of total professional experience. Previous roles include CEO and Founder at In Loco and Founder and CEO at ubee. Based in San Francisco Bay Area [US].

---

Proving you're human shouldn't require an eyeball scanner.

Most proof of humanity solutions go straight to biometrics. Scan an iris, get a credential.

But a credential ages the moment it's captured.

It can be handed off. It can be spoofed. And it only tells you who someone was at the moment they scanned, not who controls the account today.

We think the stronger signal has been there the whole time.

Real people have homes.
They have routines.
They commute, sleep, and run errands.

Over weeks and months, those behaviors create a physical signature that's statistically unique and nearly impossible to fake at scale.

A device farm running 10,000 accounts can't generate 10,000 distinct, internally consistent location histories going back months.

A bot doesn't have a morning commute.

Today we're introducing the Physical Presence Score, a continuous, privacy-preserving attestation that a device is held by a real, unique human moving through the real world.

No orb, no enrollment, nothing asked of the user.

## Startup Overview

This platform authenticates digital identities by validating the physical device and the user interaction simultaneously. It processes verification requests directly on the local device, analyzing typing patterns, screen pressure, and swipe mechanics in real time. By linking these behavioral biometrics to cryptographic hardware attestations, the system guarantees a legitimate, live human user controls the session.

Fraud and security teams deploy the engine to block synthetic identities and sophisticated presentation attacks. Legacy verification relies on static document scans or server-side facial recognition, leaving platforms vulnerable to camera injection scripts and deepfaked credentials. This solution replaces manual ID checks and risky server uploads by executing the authentication loop entirely within the local trusted execution environment.

Unlike Jumio or Socure, which depend on cloud-based evaluation of easily manipulated image payloads, this architecture is fully automated at the edge. Because the verification continuously cross-references behavioral biometrics against immutable hardware keystores locally, the system is fundamentally immune to injection attacks. The result is instant, continuous identity assurance that scales without expanding the attack surface.
